newsitem.title: USA: Ontario Hydro nuclear units resume output Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro nuclear units resume output Thursday.

text.p: Two 540 megawatt (MW) nuclear power units were expected to resume power Thursday at Ontario Hydro's Pickering, Ont., power plant after being shut for repairs, a company spokesman said.
"One of (the units) is back and the other should be back this afternoon," company spokesman Ted Gruetzner said Thursday.
The units were taken off line over the weekend for repairs, Gruetzner said. He would not be specific about the nature of those repairs.
Prior to this weekend's shutdown, Ontario Hydro had been operating four 540 MW units at the Pickering plant, located east of Toronto, Ont. The plant is made up of eight 540 MW units.
Another unit at the plant is expected to begin producing electricity in mid-September, and a sixth is expected to be on line in mid-October, Gruetzner said.
No timetable has been set to restart the remaining two units, the spokesman said.
All of the Pickering units were shut April 20 due to a problem with a backup valve on an emergency coolant system.
The Pickering plant represents about 19 percent of Ontario Hydro's total 33,000 MW generation capacity.
Also, a 930 MW nuclear unit at the Darlington power plant east of Toronto is in planned maintenance until September 16. The Darlington unit was shut down August 23, Gruetzner said.
Some of the company's electricity is sold into Michigan and other U.S. states.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
